name: show
description: Show the person something on their screen, beside your text answer: a list of blocks, each a component of the screen with its properties, drawn one under the other (at most 16). Use it when an arrangement says it better than text: a comparison as a table or cards, a diagram, a diff, figures, a picture of a file you shared. Short answers and ordinary sentences stay in your text. It is not for a file the person should keep: share that with `share_file`, and show a picture of it by naming its sha256 (the line `share_file` returns gives it) in an `Image` block, when the screen has one. It is not for a question either: a `Choices` form drawn here has nobody to answer it, so `show` refuses it. Ask with `ask_user`, which takes `choices`. The person sees the blocks as a surface beside your answer, and they stay on the screen. Call `ui_catalog` first to learn the components and their properties; a block that breaks a component's schema is refused with the reason, and you can correct it. The result is "Shown to the person.", and you still answer in text. Example: {"title": "Test run", "blocks": [{"component": "Callout", "tone": "warning", "title": "Two tests fail", "text": "Both are in the parser; I am fixing them."}]}
